Paper Title: MMBS: Towards Robust Visual Question Answering: Making the Most of Biased Samples via Contrastive Learning
Authors: Qingyi Si, Yuanxin Liu, Fandong Meng, Zheng Lin, Peng Fu, Yanan Cao, Weiping Wang, Jie Zhou
Problem Addressed: Trade-off between OOD and ID accuracy when penalizing biased samples
Method & NLP Mechanism: InfoNCE contrastive loss on positive samples generated via word Shuffling (random permutation) and prefix Removal (string deletion)
Dataset & Backbones: VQA-CP v2, VQA v2 | UpDn, BAN, LXMERT, LMH, SAR
Main Result: UpDn+MMBS: 48.19% on OOD (+8.45%), 63.84% on ID. LMH+MMBS: 56.44% on OOD, 61.87% on ID (+5.52%).
Inherent Limitation: Random word shuffling breaks syntax; prefix removal creates headless fragments. UpDn+MMBS drops from 48.19% to 42.80% on natural test questions.
What did this paper leave unresolved?: How to eliminate question category priors without corrupting the grammatical syntax and sequential transition dynamics of the language model?
Takeaway for Project Direction: Anchor Paper establishing the OOD/ID dilemma; highlights the critical need for syntax-preserving sample transformation.

Paper Title: DDG: Digging out Discrimination Information from Generated Samples for Robust Visual Question Answering
Authors: Zhiquan Wen, Yaowei Wang, Mingkui Tan, Qingyao Wu, Qi Wu
Problem Addressed: Critiques MMBS: word shuffling and removal destroy question grammar and semantics
Method & NLP Mechanism: Multi-modal Knowledge Distillation transferring discrimination information from positive/negative samples rather than rigid latent contrast
Dataset & Backbones: VQA-CP v2, VQA v2 | UpDn, SAN
Main Result: 61.14% (UpDn) and 55.52% (SAN) on VQA-CP v2; 65.54% on VQA v2 val. Checkpoint eval: 61.22%.
Inherent Limitation: Still feeds syntactically corrupted question strings into the network; relies on distillation loss to smooth over the noise.
What did this paper leave unresolved?: Bypassed the linguistic destruction with distillation rather than repairing question syntax at the input source.
Takeaway for Project Direction: Verifies that grammar destruction is a recognized bottleneck, but attempts to fix it at the loss level rather than NLP parsing.

Paper Title: Robust Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Methods, and Future Challenges
Authors: Jie Ma, Pinghui Wang, Dechen Kong, Zewei Wang, Jun Liu, Hongbin Pei, Junzhou Zhao
Problem Addressed: Lack of unified theoretical framework and taxonomy across VQA debiasing research
Method & NLP Mechanism: Comprehensive taxonomy categorizing methods into Ensemble, Data-Balanced, Causal, and Contrastive branches (MMBS as anchor)
Dataset & Backbones: All VQA Benchmarks (VQA-CP v2, GQA-OOD, VQA v2)
Main Result: Formalizes the OOD/ID trade-off dilemma and establishes standardized comparative baselines across the entire field.
Inherent Limitation: Survey paper providing analytical taxonomies without introducing a new empirical mechanism.
What did this paper leave unresolved?: Points out that the community is trapped in an artificial trade-off without a method that eliminates priors while preserving natural language.
Takeaway for Project Direction: Authoritative proof that contrastive debiasing is an enduring paradigm, and that the OOD/ID trade-off is an active open problem.

Paper Title: DSI: Dual-Space Intervention for Mitigating Bias in Robust Visual Question Answering
Authors: Runmin Wang, Xingdong Song, Zukun Wan, Han Xu, Congzhen Yu, Tianming Ma, Yajun Ding, Shengyou Qian
Role: Modern Frontier (Đỉnh cao kế thừa xáo từ)
Problem Addressed: Conflates dataset-level distribution shift with instance-level linguistic bias
Method & NLP Mechanism: Dual-Space Intervention: (1) Adaptive Question Shuffling (difficulty-mapped token shuffling) for language bias; (2) Label Rebalancing for distribution bias
Dataset & Backbones: VQA-CP v2, VQA-CP v1, VQA-CE, SLAKE-CP | UpDn
Main Result: 63.14% (VQA-CP v1), 37.61% (SLAKE-CP), SOTA on VQA-CP v2 with UpDn (>62%).
Inherent Limitation: Adaptive shuffling still performs random token permutations (torch.randperm), destroying natural question syntax, grammatical dependency edges, and sequential semantics.
What did this paper leave unresolved?: Directly inherits MMBS word shuffling but optimizes only the shuffling ratio; fails to eliminate priors while preserving natural language grammar.
Takeaway for Project Direction: Demonstrates that modern 2026 SOTA still relies on destructive word shuffling to break language priors, fully validating our syntax-preserving pure-NLP gap.
